perf_note: d1_fast = the D1 base cell (m2_first_cell_rwkv7.json) + the GPU-gated step fixes (job-2amiy, jobs/perf_step_gate rule perf_step_gate v1; stack/rwkv7/perf-step @953f3ac): row_plan min_cost 6.58 s/step (1.20x), + cont_plan single 6.11 (1.29x, peak 63 GB), + compile_blocks 5.63 (1.40x, peak 63 GB) vs greedy 7.89 on the same box. execution_note: job-tvuat (jobs/cell_step_profile, rule v1-A2, PR #86 @54ee89d) ADOPT: chosen ckpt_rows_lean = per-block activation checkpointing keeping the cache fork, the step's 8 rows batched in length-sorted groups (<= 8 rows, <= 8,192 padded tokens per call; long rows split a step into several groups), chunked_lean WKV (our pure-PyTorch rearrangement of the vendored chunked WKV, CPU-equivalence-tested; no GPU gate needed); measured median step 8.25 s, 0 OOMs, projection 1,382 steps / 11,056 rows in 190 min (receipt receipts/2026-10-07-D-cell-step-profile-tvuat). Execution flags are not in the TrainConfig hash (same loss and gradients). rwkv7_wkv applies to both arms (child: run_cell / m2_gates; parent: score_parent). 'fla' only after jobs/fla_rwkv7 ADOPT + GPU_VERIFIED.
max_minutes_note: Clock cut 780 -> 400 to fit the org's 900-min job ceiling (job_max_duration_ceiling_minutes). Cell 492 = 400 train + 42 tokenize + 10 smoke/ladder + 10 dev cards + 30 ckpt/margin. ~2,800-3,750 steps = ~23k-30k items. training wall-clock inside the 872-min cell phase = 780 train + load/draw/tokenize 42 (100k rows, as D10) + smoke+ladder 10 + two dev cards 10 + checkpoints/margin 30 (~15-19 checkpoints at ckpt_every 400; an r256 checkpoint carries ~13.8 GB of LoRA + Adam state vs ~3.5 GB at r64). Step estimate: d1_fast 5.63 s x (6.58/6.11 per_group) x 1.06 (r256) ~= 6.4 s at D1's mean T 604; v3w rows on the 100k draw are longer (mean T ~800) so ~8.5 s if step time scales with padded tokens -> ~5,500-7,300 steps = ~44k-58k items trained, ~30-40 % of the ~145k items the 100k draw renders under v3w (one pass over those rows, not over the draw). max_steps 9,000 binds only below 5.2 s/step, so the clock is the stop. Cumulative over restarts (train_clock in cell.json)
min_steps_note: exit 26 if the measured step time cannot reach 600 optimiser steps (4,800 rows) inside max_minutes: below that the cell is not a meaningful first measurement; re-price instead of spending the evals
lora_rank_note: D11: rank 256 (alpha = rank, scale 1, as D5 d5_r256); memory in memory_note. M2_RUN_SPEC r=256 adds ~1.15B trainable params (~18 GB of fp32 weights + grads + Adam) on top of 26.5 GB bf16 weights and the un-checkpointed cache-fork activations; r=64 (the pilot's pre-registered rank) keeps the T=2048 ladder rung inside the 76 GB stop
train_max_k_note: D8 code (#221 on agent-main): K cap of the training items only (train.run_cell.train_max_k; cell_items default, also used by the m2_gates lineage rebuild); max_k 16 remains the eval cap (train.m2_gates.unit_spec, run_cell eval_items). B1 100k-v2 carries rows with > 16 options (BANKING77 77-option catalogs, Glaive catalog views K 17-27), which max_k 16 alone would drop.
row_options_note: execution guard (train.trainer.row_groups / single_cont_fits): <= 160 forked continuations per backbone call; a row with K > 160 runs alone, and a step whose summed K exceeds 160 runs per group under cont_plan single. Worst call = 8,192 prefix tokens + 160 copies ~= 53.8 GB (tvuat ladder 1,024 rung) + 80 x <= 87 MB ~= 61 GB < 76 GB stop (D8 sizing). Not in the TrainConfig hash; never binds on K <= 16 steps (8 x 16 = 128).
format_note: readout-format swap point (coordinator 2026-10-08): template / layout (and r1_format_commit) are the ONLY keys that select the format; data, flags, caps and job_params are format-independent. v3w swap = once B's d3_v3w_fast code (training renderer for jrt-rwkv-g1-v3w in heads.layout / train.data, score_parent's G1V3Backend(mode='words') parent branch, decide_backend identity, check_g1v2_train_equivalence --template v3w) is merged into this branch, set template jrt-rwkv-g1-v3w (layout as B's d3_v3w_fast) in both D10 cell JSONs, re-run the census (T > 2,048 share, items by K) and the train==readout check, re-package; caps unchanged unless the census shows rows materially longer.
memory_note: r256 adds ~13.8 GB of fp32 LoRA weights + grads + Adam (LoRA params 288M -> 1,151M, 4.6 -> 18.4 GB; train.estimate, D5 @90be840). cont_plan single peaks at 63 GB at T 2,048 on r64 (job-2amiy) -> 63 + 13.8 = 76.8 GB > the 76 GB pass_rule stop: does NOT fit. cont_plan per_group (one continuation call per length-sorted group) peaks at ~54 GB on r64 (job-tvuat ckpt_rows_lean measured 49.8) -> ~67.8 GB (63.6 on the tvuat figure), ~8 GB headroom. The K > 16 path (D8 sizing): worst call 8,192 prefix tokens + row_options forked copies ~61 GB at 160 on r64 -> 74.8 GB with r256 (1.2 GB headroom, an estimate); row_options 128 drops 32 x <= 87 MB = 2.8 GB -> ~72 GB. The census max K is 77 (BANKING77), so no single row exceeds 128 and the cap only splits multi-row K > 16 groups. Execution-only (cont_plan, row_options are not in the TrainConfig hash). Cost: per_group gives back single-cont's ~8 % (job-2amiy 6.58 -> 6.11 s), and r256 adds ~6 % step FLOPs.
